Markets rally on strong earnings reports

John Smith July 11, 2026

Global equity markets rallied sharply on Friday as a wave of corporate earnings surprised to the upside, reinforcing investor confidence that the economic expansion still has room to run.

The S&P 500 gained 1.2 per cent in early trading, while the Stoxx Europe 600 added 0.8 per cent. Technology stocks led the advance after several major companies reported revenue growth that exceeded Wall Street expectations.

“We are seeing a broad-based improvement in corporate profitability,” said Sarah Chen, chief strategist at Global Asset Management. “The earnings season is shaping up to be much better than feared.”

In Europe, banking shares also performed well after stress test results showed the sector is well capitalised. German and French lenders posted some of the biggest gains.

Bond markets were relatively subdued, with the 10-year US Treasury yield rising 3 basis points to 4.15 per cent as investors rotated into risk assets. The dollar index was flat against a basket of major currencies.

Analysts cautioned that the rally could be tested next week when a fresh batch of economic data is released, including inflation figures and retail sales numbers.
